name: yamaha_cp2_689
label: Yamaha CP2 689 cc 270° parallel twin (MT-07)
based_on: Yamaha CP2 689 cc parallel twin, MT-07 / FZ-07, 2014 on

sources.what: FIA homologation form 2023-06-XCAR-MT07, 'XC Engine YAMAHA MT07 2016-2023' (36 pages, valid from 23/06/2023): measured dimensions of the stock engine for cross-car racing: rod length, valve sizes, cam lobe dimensions, cam lift table, lobe centres, max valve lift, throttle bore. Regulator document; the best public geometry source found.

Yamaha FZ-07 (FZ07F / FZ07FC, 2015 US model) owner's manual LIT-11626-28-55 / 2RC-28199-1R, PDF mirrored on maintenanceschedule.com: bore x stroke, displacement, compression ratio, tachometer red zone.
Yamaha Motor Europe 2020 MT-07 factsheet PDF (yamaha-motor.eu CDN): power, torque, bore x stroke, compression, 270-degree crank with uneven firing interval. Manufacturer primary source.

totalmotorcycle.com 2015 FZ-07 page reproducing Yamaha's feature copy and spec tables: valve sizes and angles, 38 mm throttle body, 2-into-1 exhaust, balancer, 7 mm cylinder offset. Manufacturer text on a third-party page.
Yamaha Motor global technology page on the 270-degree crank: origin of the layout and confirmation that the MT-07 uses it. No numbers beyond 270 degrees.
Wikipedia, Straight-twin engine: definition of the 270-degree crank and its 270/450 firing intervals, naming the MT-07 as an example.
motofomo.com article on the CP2 engine: states 270/450 intervals for the CP2 specifically. Enthusiast site, cites Yamaha material loosely; used only as a second voice for the intervals.
Wikipedia, Yamaha MT-07: cross-check of bore, stroke, compression, power and a rear-wheel dyno figure.

notes: Sourced: bore, stroke, compression ratio, parallel twin with a 270-degree crank (Yamaha's factsheet), firing intervals 270/450 (Wikipedia's straight-twin article, which names this engine), rod length 124 mm (FIA homologation form), four valves per cylinder, valve diameters 31.5/26.5 mm, valve lift 7.6 mm, lobe centres 111 (intake) and 112 (exhaust) degrees, cam lift table, 38 mm throttle bodies, 2-into-1 exhaust, red zone 10,000 rpm, published power and torque. Assumed: which cylinder fires 270 degrees after the other. The research file's firing order '1-2' has no source and no page says which cylinder leads; cylinder 1 is taken to fire first. It changes nothing in the sound of a 2-into-1 exhaust with equal pipes. Derived by calculation, not published: valve timing at 1 mm lift (intake opens 6 after TDC, closes 37 after BDC; exhaust opens 38 before BDC, closes 6 before TDC). It comes from the FIA cam lift table (measured with a 3 mm ball on the bare camshaft), converted to flat-tappet lift assuming bucket tappets and that the table is in camshaft degrees, less the minimum valve clearance, and placed on the sourced lobe centres. Estimated, not sourced: idle speed (1350 rpm); intake length (0.17 m) and diameter; exhaust primary length (0.63 m) and diameter, collector, silencer and tailpipe dimensions; flywheel inertia; friction_scale 0.6, heat_q 2.7e6 and burn_scale 0.7, the first two at the end of their allowed range.

vehicle.name: Yamaha MT-07 (2014)
vehicle.notes: curb_kg is Yamaha Europe's wet weight for the non-ABS MT-07 (182 kg with ABS). gears and final_drive come from the 2015 US FZ-07 owner's manual, the same bike sold under its US name; the EU secondary ratio (2.688) is confirmed by MOTORRAD, the EU internal and primary ratios are assumed identical. final_drive is primary 77:40 x chain 43:16. top_speed_kmh is Yamaha's claim as quoted by MOTORRAD. wheel_radius_m is calculated from the tyre size.
